solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sweet given Her Majesty’s approval, perhaps a moneymaker

blocks.note: royal = favoured by the monarch, as in 'by royal appointment'
a mint is a sweet

explanation.surface: A confection that has earned the Queen's seal of approval, and might even make its maker rich.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Mint is the body that makes British coins, so 'perhaps' flags a punning example: a moneymaker in the most literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Mint literally manufactures money, so it is one example of a moneymaker.

clue.text: Teacher’s upset, being given single meatball

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is turned upside down

blocks.note: pupils call a male teacher sir
sole = only, single

explanation.surface: A teacher is put out at being served one lonely meatball for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the teacher is upset, turned upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a small ball or cake of minced meat, fried.

clue.text: Variable? I hesitate to say, I like it!

blocks.note: y is a standard algebraic variable
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone pauses before admitting that they actually enjoy something unpredictable.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematicians' x, y and z are the usual variables; y is the one needed here.
explanation.definitionFit: Yum is the exclamation of someone enjoying food: 'I like it!'

clue.text: Top-class Olympic venue reluctant at first to identify seducer

blocks.note: loth (or loath) = reluctant
A = first-rate, as in grade A
Rio de Janeiro hosted the 2016 Olympics

explanation.surface: Someone at a smart Olympic site is hesitant to name the person who led them astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue order is A, RIO, LOTH, but 'at first' moves LOTH to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothario, from a Restoration play, is a byword for a charming seducer of women.

clue.text: Expose oneself to copper wearing hip designer’s latest

blocks.note: in = fashionable, hip
Cu is copper's chemical symbol
the last letter of designer

explanation.surface: A flasher strips off before a policeman while dressed in the newest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip designer's latest' reads as one fashionable label, but it splits into two pieces, with the copper worn between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: you incur debts or anger when your own actions leave you open to them.

clue.text: Process intended to avoid a course of drugs

blocks.note: to treat is to process, as with chemicals
meant = intended
the letter A taken out of MEANT

explanation.surface: A procedure designed to keep someone off a drug programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Process' is not the definition: it is a verb giving TREAT, and the real definition sits at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a prescribed course of drugs is one kind of medical care, alongside surgery or physiotherapy.

clue.text: Revolutionary man of the cloth, one swapping with European

blocks.note: linen is a cloth
I = one, the Roman numeral
E = European

explanation.surface: A rebellious priest who changes places with someone from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man of the cloth' wants to be a clergyman; split it as 'Revolutionary man' plus 'the cloth'. Swapping I and E turns LINEN into LENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Russian Revolution of 1917.

clue.text: Famous Liverpudlian flag, 50 for a penny

blocks.note: a pennon is a long narrow flag
L is the Roman numeral for 50
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A Merseyside celebrity is sold a flag for a mere 50, or a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: PENNON, with its P swapped for L, becomes LENNON.
explanation.definitionFit: John Lennon of the Beatles was born in Liverpool.

clue.text: Keep on smooching, being very close

blocks.note: British slang for kissing and cuddling, and 'keep on' asks for it twice over
level in a race, with neither ahead

explanation.walkthrough: To neck is British slang for to kiss and cuddle, so 'neck and neck' can be read as smooching without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck and neck describes a race so close that neither side leads.

clue.text: Case of Navajo and the sleep that never ends? Most curious!

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
a siesta that never ends is missing its final letter

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Navajo
a siesta is an afternoon sleep

explanation.surface: Someone wonders at a Navajo legend of eternal sleep and finds it very strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sleep that never ends' sounds like death, but it is SIESTA losing its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Curious here means inquisitive, so most curious is nosiest.

clue.text: Prophet rejected peculiar feature of the body

blocks.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet
a tic is an odd habitual twitch or quirk

explanation.surface: A prophet is turned away because of some strange mark on his body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature of the body' looks like the definition, but 'feature' belongs with 'peculiar'; the definition is 'of the body'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somatic means relating to the body, as opposed to the mind.

clue.text: They mind the sultanas not being whole

definitions.text: They mind the sultanas not being whole

blocks.note: sultanas here are not dried grapes but a sultan's wives, and to mind them is to guard the harem
the guards were castrated, so not whole men

explanation.walkthrough: Sultanas are dried fruit to the grocer, but here they are sultans' wives, and 'not being whole' describes their castrated guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eunuchs guarded the harems of Ottoman sultans.

clue.text: Painter drawn to East End longing for some theatrics

indicators.note: Cockneys from London's East End drop their H, so 'hope' becomes 'ope

blocks.note: hope = longing
RA = Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist is pulled towards the East End of London, craving drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the working-class district of London whose Cockney speech drops the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is theatre at its most dramatic, so 'some theatrics' fits.

clue.text: Idiot fiancé prepared for instruction

indicators.note: the letters are prepared, worked into a new shape

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

explanation.surface: A foolish husband-to-be gets ready to be taught something.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on fiancé is ignored, as crossword convention allows.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though a lofty one: it is instruction that improves the mind or morals.

clue.text: Restrict supply of booze? There’s a reason

blocks.note: to ration is to restrict supply
ale is beer

explanation.surface: Someone justifies cutting back the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two parts: the supply being rationed is the ale.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the reasoning that lies behind a decision.

clue.text: Get rid of priest, worried about mind finally failing

blocks.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel
loses its final D
to eat someone is to worry them: what's eating you?

explanation.surface: An anxious priest is dismissed as his mind finally goes.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli, the biblical priest, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: knocking out rivals or errors means removing them entirely.

clue.text: I am a droll, outlandish creature

indicators.note: the letters are made strange and foreign, so rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A strange beast introduces itself as a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the creature speaking about itself, which hides that 'I am a droll' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Make changes to what one eats, promoting energy

blocks.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
your diet is what you eat; its E moves up

explanation.surface: Someone overhauls their meals to boost their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: In DIET the E is third; promoting it to the head gives EDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a verb: what editors do to a text before it is published.

clue.text: Henry breaking policeman’s teeth

blocks.note: copper = policeman, with the 's
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone called Henry knocks a policeman's teeth out.
explanation.walkthrough: A copper is British slang for a policeman. Choppers is informal for teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Choppers is jocular British slang for teeth.

clue.text: British soldier back in prison

blocks.note: Br is the abbreviation for British
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A British soldier finds himself back behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British soldier' wants to be a single unit such as a Tommy; in fact the soldier is American, and British is only the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The brig is a ship's prison, and in US slang a military prison.

clue.text: Apparently retired city bishops spilt the beans

blocks.note: someone who has retired has, apparently, gone to bed
LA = Los Angeles
B is bishop in chess notation; BB is two of them

explanation.surface: Bishops who have supposedly stepped down reveal a city's secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: No word says 'around': the setter lets the bed simply enclose the city and the bishops, so the container is implied.
explanation.definitionFit: To blab is to spill the beans, reveal a secret.

clue.text: Unique reason for not lighting up?

blocks.note: without a match, an equal
with no match you cannot light your cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: being match-less, without a match, is why you cannot light your cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means without equal, unique.

clue.text: Top chap riding white horses well?

blocks.note: the uppermost face or layer of something
white horses are waves breaking into foam, and a chap who rides them well is an expert at that sport

explanation.walkthrough: White horses are waves breaking into foam, or surf, so a chap who rides them well is a surf ace.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a plain synonym for the uppermost face; the second is a cryptic phrase that splits the word into two.

clue.text: It makes a loud noise and it smells

blocks.note: a horn or siren, like a factory's
the nose, in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: A hooter is a horn or siren, and in British slang also a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory hooter makes a loud noise; your hooter, the nose, is what smells.

clue.text: Cold-blooded customers can make a canon sad

indicators.note: the letters can be made into something else

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Heartless shoppers are able to upset a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded customers' reads as callous people; a customer is also just a character, here a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: Anacondas are snakes, reptiles, and so literally cold-blooded.

clue.text: Doctor has to sleep over in empty synagogue

indicators.note: in a down clue, over turns the word upside down

blocks.note: the first and last letters of synagogue
kip is British slang for a sleep

explanation.surface: A doctor needs a nap and bunks down in a deserted synagogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here: to spike a drink is to doctor it.
explanation.definitionFit: To spike a drink is to doctor it by adding something.

clue.text: Permissible in each game

blocks.note: per = each, as in 'per head'
OK = acceptable, permissible

explanation.surface: Something is allowed in every match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permissible' looks like the start of a definition, but it is the inner piece and 'game' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: poker is one card game among many, played for stakes.

clue.text: Riots flaring in the middle of Dublin’s port

blocks.note: the middle two letters of DUBLIN
anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out in the heart of the Irish capital's harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dublin's port' looks like it wants an Irish port such as Dun Laoghaire; the definition is 'port' alone and the answer is English.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a historic port city in the west of England.

clue.text: Strike ban announcement covering particular craft

indicators.note: the words cover, that is contain, the answer

blocks.note: strIKE BAN Announcement

explanation.surface: A declaration that walkouts are banned, covering one trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all industrial relations, with 'craft' suggesting a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of flower arranging, a particular craft.

clue.text: Woman’s wedding announcement removed from case

indicators.note: the case, the outer letters, is taken off, leaving the inside

blocks.note: BANNS without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman's marriage notice is taken out of its display cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: The banns are the church announcement of a coming wedding; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one particular woman's name standing for any woman, a common crossword device.

clue.text: One who dishes out fast food to audience

indicators.note: what the audience hears is the sound, not the spelling

blocks.note: a doner kebab is a British takeaway staple

explanation.surface: A takeaway worker serves up quick meals to a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A doner kebab is the late-night takeaway of spiced meat carved from a spit; doner and donor sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who hands over money, organs or blood, as a server dishes out food.

clue.text: I see Bacon wrongly getting great respect

indicators.note: the letters are put wrongly, out of their order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Someone admits misjudging Francis Bacon, who is now held in high esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon the philosopher or painter, with its capital, disguises plain anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeisance is deep respect, or a bow expressing it.
